assessment: This study investigates evolutionary changes in ligand preference that occur in an olfactory receptor (IR75a) across the Drosophila phylogeny. The authors find that IR75a displays different odor preferences, for acetic acid or butyric acid, across Drosophila species, and link odor preference to particular protein mutations in the receptor. Reconstruction of a putative ancestral IR75a revises the timeline for IR75a evolution, and structural modeling suggests how mutations alter odor preference.
